opinions.rationale: The claim asserts that 'No procedure bounds the resulting bias from quantities available before the analysis,' which reads as a structural impossibility. However, the report's own proposed direction ('Derive the bias in the comparator hazard as a function of the three quantities an analyst knows before sampling... it should yield a bound') demonstrates that the problem is not structurally impossible but rather a gap in current methodology. The claim is overstated, wearing the language of impossibility for what is actually an absence of a standard procedure. I abstain on the status axis because I cannot verify whether such a procedure has already been derived in the literature.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: No currently established procedure bounds the resulting bias from quantities available before the analysis, so the scheme is picked by convention and its consequences are read off afterward, one dataset at a time.
